title: Quenched Mustardy Norwegian Vegetables Bake
description: A date-night Norwegian dish featuring the crunch of fresh vegetables and the tang of mustard, all wrapped up in a rich vanilla-scented sauce.
instructions: Toss the cabbage, carrots, and parsnips with the olive oil, salt, and black pepper on a large baking sheet.
Roast the vegetables in the preheated oven for 25 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned.
In a small saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the flour and whisk to combine, cooking for 1 minute.
Slowly pour in the apple cider vinegar and Dijon mustard, whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in the vanilla extract and grated cheddar cheese until melted and smooth.
To assemble the bake, place the roasted vegetables in a 9x13 inch baking dish and spoon the mustard sauce over the top.
Transfer the dish to the oven and bake for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the sauce is bubbly and the flavors are well combined.
Let the bake rest for 5 minutes before serving, allowing the sauce to set.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.
Baked vegetables may be refrigerated for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 2 months.
To reheat, thaw frozen vegetables overnight in the refrigerator and bake in a preheated oven at 375°F (190°C) for 20-25 minutes, or until hot and bubbly.
